texts.facts: In this writ petition, petitioner has submitted that it is high time to direct the respondents to act in tune with Article 47 of the Constitution of India and to create public awareness system by constituting a body for the same with appropriate directions to monitor various products marketed in the country, the health hazards caused by the said products and also create awareness of fake and spurious materials which are sold in public as a substitute for authentic products and thereby save the life of the people. WP(C) NO. 24827 OF 2022 :: 3 :: 3. It is submitted by the petitioner that he is having large plantation of Cinnamon in his hometown in Kannur District wherein, he cultivates cinnamon for the last more than ten years. In the year 2015, he noticed that instead of cinnamon another product namely 'Cassia' imported from other countries were marketed in Kerala as a substitute for cinnamon. 4. Being aggrieved by this, petitioner has filed several complaints and thereafter, filed writ petition before this court seeking to ban sale of cassia in the country. This court, while considering the writ petition, has directed the third respondent - State of Kerala to inform the court whether it had taken any steps of prohibit sale of cassia in Kerala.
texts.arguments: (ii) Issue writ of mandamus or any other writ or order directing the respondents 1 to 3 to constitute a body to create a public awareness system to implement the directions in the directive principles of state policy under the Article 47 of the Constitution of India. 5. Main grievance of the petitioner is that there is inaction on the part of the respondents to create awareness to improve the health of the public and encourage them to avoid the unhealthy products available in the market. Article 47 of the Constitution mandates the State shall take all endeavor to create public awareness and that it is the duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and WP(C) Leonard John vs The Union Of India on 3 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139395107/ 2 NO. 24827 OF 2022 :: 4 :: standard of living and to improve public health as among their primary duties and State shall endeavor to bring about prohibition of consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs which are injurious to health except for medicinal purpose. 6. Petitioner has submitted that the right to health is a fundamental right guaranteed under the Article 21 of the Constitution. It is the duty of the respondents to see that there is no presence of pesticides or any substance hazardous to health in the products supplied in the market whether it is food or medicine. It is also submitted that the Government is duty bound to spend a reasonable portion of funds on publicity for the purpose of creating awareness to the public about the health hazard caused by these fake and spurious products.
